arguments.summary: No dated primary trade-policy/restriction document was available after the BIS-policy source failed. The only documented watchlist transmission channel is QQQ’s dated look-through to NVDA, MU and META; direct company exposure and policy impact remain unquantified.

claims.text: QQQ’s supplied holdings table dated 2026-09-12 includes NVDA (8.45%), MU (4.85%) and META (3.07%); therefore, any documented policy shock to those constituents could transmit indirectly to QQQ. The table is marked stale and does not establish current weights or company-specific policy impact.

Arista’s latest available 10-Q describes wholly owned subsidiaries throughout North America, Europe, Asia and Australia, documenting cross-border operations but not a country revenue split, supplier concentration, or a restriction-specific exposure.

Over 21/63 sessions, a newly enacted or enforced trade restriction affecting advanced compute, memory, networking equipment, or cross-border technology supply could affect directly exposed issuers through shipments, sourcing, customer demand, or compliance costs, and QQQ indirectly through constituent holdings. This is a transmission scenario, not a quantified loss estimate or direction-of-price call.

gaps.description: No retrievable dated primary BIS/trade-policy material establishes the current restriction, proposal/enactment/enforcement status, covered products/countries, or issuer-specific financial effect.

Latest company filing excerpts supplied here do not quantify China/other cross-border revenue, restricted-product exposure, Taiwan/Asian manufacturing reliance, or supplier/customer mitigation for MU, META, or NVDA; ANET evidence only documents international subsidiaries.
QQQ holdings are dated 2026-09-12 and marked stale; QQQ has no policy-exposure or sector-weight breakdown in supplied data.

assumptions: A future policy action would be material only if it covers products, countries, or counterparties relevant to a constituent; that mapping is not established by available evidence.
QQQ look-through is limited to the dated reported constituent weights and is not an allocation recommendation.
arguments.counter_thesis: Absent a newly documented restriction or company disclosure, policy headlines may have no material operational effect within 21/63 sessions; the supplied record cannot establish that any issuer is directly exposed.

review_conditions.description: Review upon a dated primary trade-policy release or issuer filing that identifies covered technology/country and quantifies revenue, supply-chain, shipment, or compliance exposure.

question_effects.reason: Company-exposure question was routed but no response is available in this task; supplied excerpts do not quantify direct exposure.

shared_exposures.mechanism: QQQ has dated reported constituent holdings in NVDA, MU and META, so company-level trade-policy effects could transmit to the ETF.
shared_exposures.qualification: Weights are as of 2026-09-12 and the holdings feed is marked stale; this does not establish current fund exposure, policy sensitivity, or a portfolio recommendation.
